title: Instrumentation decision lattice + dashboard surgery notes
content:
Purpose:
This is a working decision lattice for instrumentation and a compact set of dashboard surgery notes targeted at reducing query costs while keeping investigation fidelity for token-serving incidents. Goal is pragmatic: preserve key investigation paths, cut low-value high-cardinality signals, and provide a repeatable rubric for future features (model variants, routing, caching).

Context and motivation:
- We keep getting high-cost dashboards during P99 latency spikes because people add high-cardinality histograms for every tag (tenant, model, route, prompt-type).
- New Dedicated customers require tighter SLOs and predictable dashboards (query budgets).
- We want an express decision process (a lattice) to decide when to add a metric vs rely on traces or sampled spans.

Decision lattice (quick guide):
(1) Is this a routing-critical signal (affects request path or fallback)? --> YES: instrument as a counter + trace tag.
(2) Does it require per-tenant granularity for billing/alerts? --> YES: counter + per-tenant rollup metric (low-cardinality) + sampled trace for deep dive.
(3) Is the cardinality > 50 distinct values per minute (e.g., prompt_id, user_text fingerprint)? --> YES: avoid full metric; use trace-enriched attribute and synthetic probes.
(4) Is it correlated with token-cost or cache-warmth? --> YES: store as timeseries but aggregate to heatmap-bucket (cold/warm/partial) not per-request tag.
(5) If unsure, prefer a sampled span annotation and 24-72h trace retention in the sandbox dataset for investigation.

Metric naming conventions (proposal):
- <area>.<object>.<measurement> (snake_case). Example: serving.kv_cache.hit_rate_1m, serving.request.latency_p50_ms.
- Use suffixes for aggregation window: _1m, _5m, _1h.
- Avoid embedding tenant IDs in series names; use labels/tags instead and only rollup to tenant-level for pre-approved metrics.

Proposed metric definitions (high-priority):
1) serving.kv_cache.hit_rate_1m
   - type: gauge (derived ratio)
   - calculation: 100 * sum(kv_cache.hits_1m) / max(1, sum(kv_cache.requests_1m))
   - owner: eng-serving-runtime
   - alert: <70% for >10m on Dedicated tiers
   - note: store as bucketed heatmap for warm/cold/partial to reduce series count

2) serving.request.latency_p99_ms
   - type: histogram-derived quantile
   - calculation: p99 over request latency (end-to-end generation completion) in last 5m windows
   - owner: eng-sre
   - alert: >SLO threshold per model-route for 5m & 15m
   - note: keep per-route, not per-prompt-type by default

3) serving.model.queue_time_sum_1m & serving.model.queue_time_count_1m
   - type: histogram components for average queue time
   - calculation: sum/count -> average queue time
   - owner: serving-runtime
   - alert: rising queue_time_concurrency correlated with throttling events

4) serving.fallback.invocations_1m (counter)
   - type: counter
   - calculation: increments when fallback to cheaper/compatible model occurs
   - owner: product-hosted-api
   - alert: >1% of traffic to fallback for 15m (user-impact check)

Tracing guidance (compact):
- Span naming: use dot-separated, stable names: generation.request -> top-level request; generation.model.call -> per-model backend; generation.kv.lookup -> cache interactions; generation.emit -> tokens sent to client.
- Attributes to always attach to top-level span (keep cardinality low): model_id, route, region, customer_tier.
- High-cardinality data (prompt_id, user_text_fingerprint, session_token) should be added as sampled attributes (sample_rate tag) or redacted in production spans.
- Sampling policy:
   - Default: probabilistic 0.5% retain rate for production across all services.
   - Error-based: 100% trace-retention for responses with status != 200 or latency > P99*1.5.
   - Customer-tier override: Dedicated customers may opt-in for 5% baseline retention for their traffic (configurable).
- Trace enrichment: attach a compact 'investigation_context' tag with a small bitmask of flags (cache_miss, model_fallback, cold_start) so operators can filter without high-cardinality fields.

Dashboard surgery notes (how to slim and keep signal):
- Always start with the Investigation Ladder (top -> bottom): SLO panel, latency waterfall, error rate & fallback rate, queue/backlog, kv-cache heatmap, span-sample viewer link. Keep that order across all model-route dashboards.
- Preferred aggregations: median/95/99 for latency; rate per-second for counters with a 1m rolling window; heatmaps for cache-warmth rather than per-tenant lines.
- Replace any per-tenant line charts with percentile-lined rollups + per-tenant sampling widget that shows a spotlight for top-n tenants only (configurable).
- Limit high-cardinality tables to a single expandable panel (collapse by default). Use precomputed top-k job to populate.
- Query budget policy: dashboards in the Observability space must be scored for expected monthly query cost. Any new widget that adds >3 high-cardinality group-bys requires a short justification and approval from eng-observability.

Investigation playbook snippets (operator-facing):
- P99 spike: open the waterfall -> check model.queue_time and model.batch_size -> inspect kv_cache.hit_rate heatmap for cold slices -> if fallback.invocations rising, check model variant rollout and routing rules.
- High error spikes: use trace sampling rules to capture 100% of error traces for 30m, then analyze span anchors: generation.model.call error/message.

Example dashboard panel layout (compact):
1. SLO status (pie & burn rate)
2. Latency timeseries (p50/p95/p99) across routes (low-cardinality)
3. Latency waterfall (queue -> model -> emit) stacked bars
4. KV cache heatmap (cold/warm/partial buckets over time)
5. Fallback rate timeseries + top_routes table (top 5)
6. Trace-sample quicklink + last-failed-span snippet

Owner matrix and onboarding checklist:
- eng-observability: metric catalog gatekeeper, dashboard query budget reviews, alert templating.
- eng-serving-runtime: owns cache metrics, model queue metrics, batching counters.
- eng-sre: SLO thresholds and paging rules.
- product-hosted-api: fallback instrumentation and feature flags.

Onboarding checklist for a new metric/dashboard panel:
- Fill out short metric stub (name, calc, owner, cardinality estimate) in /telemetry/metric-intake (Confluence)
- Run cardinality audit script (link in linked_artifacts) and capture expected series count/month
- If >10k series/month, discuss heatmap/bucket approach with eng-observability
- Create dashboard PR and include query cost estimation

Open questions / proposals:
- Proposal A: Add a compact 'cache_warmth_bucket' label with 3 states stored as a single numeric series to replace many per-request tags. (pro: low-cardinality; con: may lose nuance).
- Proposal B: Shift percentiles to pre-aggregated sketches on ingestion to lower query-time cost (requires infra changes).
- Sampling: Should we increase baseline trace retention to 1% for all hosted-api traffic for better ML-quality triage? Cost estimate needed (INF-2043).

Notes to self / loose ideas:
- Consider a dashboard-level query budget meter in the top-right of every Observability dashboard with a 'cost impact' label (green/yellow/red).
- Add a small widget that surfaces the last 10 high-cardinality queries and the owner who created them for quick follow-up.

Action items (next steps):
- [ ] Run a 7-day cardinality scan across top 20 dashboards and produce a heatmap of hot series (owner: Miguel, due: 2024-11-01).
- [ ] Prototype cache_warmth_bucket inversion in the telemetry sandbox (owner: Priya, due: 2024-11-10).
- [ ] Draft short runbook for fallback paging noise reduction (owner: Jonah, due: 2024-11-05).

References and quick links:
- Instrumentation catalog (Confluence): OBS-telemetry-catalog
- Jira: INF-2043 (sampling cost analysis)
- GitHub PR for dashboard query budget UI: github.com/redwood-inference/telemetry/pull/312

End of notes. This doc is intentionally practical and prescriptive — use it for sprint work and gate reviews. Add any related carrot/complaint threads below when iterating.
